his satchel round his shoulder, and, regardless of his mother's constantly reiterated entreaties
that he would always put on galoshes in such cold weather, he looked at them contemptuously
as he crossed the hall and went out with only his boots on.
Perezvon, seeing him in his outdoor clothes, began tapping nervously, yet vigorously on
the floor with his tail.
Twitching all over, he even uttered a plaintive whine.
But Kolya, seeing his dog's passionate excitement, decided that it was a breach of discipline,
kept him for another minute under the bench, and only when he had opened the door into
the passage, whistled for him.
The dog leapt up like a mad creature and rushed bounding before him rapturously.
